newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African population estimated at 37.9 mln people.
newsitem.headline: S.African population estimated at 37.9 mln people.

text.p: South Africa's population has been preliminary estimated at 37.9 million people, the Central Statistical Service said on Tuesday.

Announcing the preliminary results of its 1996 census, the service (CSS) said that of the total, which had been adjusted for "under-count", 18.2 million or 48 percent were male and 19.7 million (52 percent) were female.
Other data on employment, education, health and housing would be released in 1998.
It said the purpose of issuing preliminary estimates was to make selected summary data available as quickly as possible.

"In South Africa, decision-makers have lacked reliable demographic information on which to base their plans, especially during the last twenty years under apartheid when statistics for the former (nominally independent homelands) were hived off."
The CSS said it had found the results surprising given that at its last census in 1991, it had projected that South Africa's population would have grown to about 42.1 million people in 1996.
"The surprise arises because the previous 1991 counts in South Africa had been adjusted upwards to match a demographic model."

The survey found that the country's KwaZulu-Natal province was the most populated with 20.3 percent or 7.672 million people, while the Northern Cape was the most sparsely populated with 746,000 people, or two percent of the total.
